Settled as factual and true, but I give it small weight: 3-month relative momentum has near-zero predictive power at a 2-week horizon, and the most recent two weeks (QQQ +1.1% vs SPY +1.0%) show the gap no longer widening. Net of (1) and (2) the center lands essentially at the structural drift, slightly shaded down - hence +0.05, not run 2's -0.12 and not run 1/3's +0.10. (3) Sep FOMC hike odds: quoted at ~50% (run 1, post-Waller, 13bp priced) and ~65% (run 2). Factual, unsettleable without a live rates screen; either way the meeting is a two-sided dispersion event rather than a directional one, so it does not move my median, and I let the uncertainty sit in the width. (4) Oracle's index membership: run 1 asserts ORCL is NYSE-listed and NOT in the NDX (so its report would help SPX only); runs 2-3 treat it as an NDX member. Factual and NOT settleable from the dossiers - the two claims are flatly contradictory and neither carries a primary source. ORCL is one name reporting inside the window; I decline to lean on it in either direction. (5) Dispersion: runs proposed 3.2 / 3.7 / 3.53. Run 1's 3.2 is too tight given a live FOMC with a dot plot plus quad-witching inside a 9-session window; run 2's 3.7 comes from correlation as low as 0.87, which is a monthly-horizon figure. I recompute from the trailing vols and daily correlation 0.95 and get 3.57, adopting essentially run 3's width. (6) Escape mass: all three price ~1.7-2.2% total with a downside tilt, citing Jul-2024 and Feb-Mar-2025 rotations reaching ~4pp in 10 sessions; I keep that, at 1.2%/0.8%. Roll convention (adjusted vs raw front-month across the Sep 18 expiry) is unspecified in the empty criteria text and unsettleable here; it is worth only ~0.02pp and is absorbed in the center.
